# ModDotPlot Browser v0.8.9

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

v0.8.9 makes the bundled *Arabidopsis thaliana* example's indexed loading visible and
consolidates each multi-chromosome logical annotation into a single feature-track row.
The example retrieves `Col-CEN_v1.2.fasta`, its matching
`Col-CEN_v1.2.fasta.fai`, and `ColCEN_CEN180.gff3` with percentage progress. A
logical annotation no longer contributes a duplicate sidebar entry per chromosome;
its sequence-specific features automatically follow matching X and Y selections.

See the [validation record](v0.8.9/VALIDATION.md) for the release checks on this
isolated source copy.

## Indexed bundled Arabidopsis example

Select **Try ModDotPlot on an Arabadopsis genome** to retrieve all three same-origin
example assets. The landing-page progress bar reports **Downloading included
Arabidopsis genome** for aggregate streamed retrieval from 0% through 95%, then
**Reading included FASTA index** while indexed preparation completes through 100%.
The FAI is supplied to the existing indexed-input path, so
all chromosome names and lengths can become available without first packing the whole
134 MB FASTA; sequence bases are loaded on demand when a plot needs them.

The example assets are included in the release site:

* `examples/Col-CEN_v1.2.fasta`
* `examples/Col-CEN_v1.2.fasta.fai`
* `examples/ColCEN_CEN180.gff3`

This progress describes retrieval of bundled static assets. Ordinary user-selected
indexed files continue to use their existing local browser `File` references.
The example progress interface is removed on cancellation, failure, or entry into the
workspace so it cannot remain visible for a stale load.

## One logical track row across chromosomes

Importing multi-sequence BED, GFF3, or GTF data from the landing screen or **Add
track** now adds one entry per logical track name to **Feature tracks**, not one
duplicate entry per matching chromosome.
Internally, the imported features remain associated with their annotation sequence
identifiers. For each X or Y axis, the row displays the subset matching the currently
selected FASTA sequence.

For example, the bundled `ColCEN_CEN180.gff3` contains features for five chromosomes
but appears as one `ColCEN_CEN180` entry. Selecting Chr1, Chr2, or another matching
chromosome automatically uses that chromosome's features from the same track. Track
visibility, row count, ordering, and deletion are controlled once for the logical row
instead of being repeated for every chromosome. BED files that explicitly
define different `track name=` datasets continue to receive one row per distinct name.
An explicit drop on one coordinate axis remains scoped to that one axis sequence.

Exact identifier matches remain preferred, and the existing conservative chromosome
alias rules continue to apply. If the logical track has no records matching a displayed
axis sequence, its control for that axis is unavailable.

## Compatibility and rollback

Scientific estimation, exact rendering, plot/grid semantics, indexed and eager FASTA
parsing, annotation feature geometry, exports, palettes, and cursor guides are
unchanged from v0.8.8. The complete v0.8.8 source remains beside this release for
direct comparison and rollback.
